---
title: "Condition on an observed trajectory"
---

A static input is one value per realization. An observed sequence is a value
per timepoint known at prediction time, such as a prescribed intervention or
an externally supplied environmental trajectory. Do not put a changing sequence
in the static-input columns.

## Bank and model schema

Keep both observed and predicted channels in the bank's output schema, then
name the observed channels when constructing the model:

```python
from metis import SimulationDataset, Surrogate, TrainingConfig
bank = SimulationDataset.from_parquet(
    "conditioned_bank.parquet", inputs=["contact_rate"],
    outputs=["intervention", "incidence"],
)
split = bank.split(seed=42)
model = Surrogate("transformer", observed_outputs=["intervention"]).fit(
    split.train, split.validation, config=TrainingConfig(steps=500),
)
```

The bank still needs complete, aligned time grids and disjoint scenario groups.
The model learns to predict the remaining channels. In the example its output
is `incidence`; `intervention` is supplied, not generated. MLP and iTARFlow do
not support observed-sequence conditioning.

## Prediction and sampling

```python
prediction = model.predict(
    {"contact_rate": 0.4}, conditioning=known_intervention,
)
```

`known_intervention` has shape `(input settings, fitted timepoints, observed
channels)`, here `(1, T, 1)`, in original units. Its channel order follows the
`observed_outputs` declaration. Prediction returns `(B,T,C_predicted)`.
For `Surrogate("flow_matching", observed_outputs=[...])`, use
`sample(inputs, conditioning=known_sequence, n_samples=100, seed=42)` to obtain
`(B,S,T,C_predicted)`. The portable artifact preserves the conditioning schema
and scaling. Missing or incompatible shapes fail validation; an array cannot reveal
a mistaken channel order, so preserve the declared order yourself.

Hydra uses the same constructor:

```bash
uv run metis train dataset=parquet dataset.path=conditioned_bank.parquet 'dataset.inputs=[contact_rate]' 'dataset.outputs=[intervention,incidence]' model=transformer 'model.observed_outputs=[intervention]'
```

## Information available at prediction time

The autoregressive transformer uses causal attention. Flow matching processes
a full trajectory jointly, and its outputs can depend on the supplied sequence
as a whole. It is suitable for generation conditional on a known full path;
do not present this as forecasting based only on observations available so far.
Always define which quantities are known in the intended application. Held-out
evaluation cannot repair conditioning information that would be unavailable
when the model is deployed.

`model.evaluate(test_bank)` takes the same full output schema used during fit.
It extracts observed channels from each held-out run and scores only predicted
channels. The test claim is conditional performance given that supplied path;
it is not performance when that path is unknown.
